title: The point-fibre representative is unchanged by enlargement of its coefficient field
statement: Fix the finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, and an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$. Let $S$ be the coefficient stage system at $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ of [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. For pairs $A,B$ of that system, finite coefficient subfields $G\subset H\subset\Omega$, inclusions $h_A:A.stage\le G$ and $h_B:B.stage\le G$, and a stage map $f:A_G\to B_G$, let $S.\operatorname{tr}_{H/G}(f)=\alpha_A^{-1}\,T_{H/G}(f)\,\alpha_B$ be its further extension using the specified source associators. The arrow on representatives $R$ and object map $O$ are exactly [def-weil-point-fibre-stage-constructions]. Then, as morphisms $O(A)\to O(B)$ in [def-weil-point-fd-qlbar-category], $$R_H(S.\operatorname{tr}_{H/G}(f))=R_G(f).$$ No functor from the pair category and no independence of representatives is assumed.

proof.text: Normalize the small rational scalar comparison by its defining equation after the fully faithful module carrier lift. The sections tower equation and the pure-tensor tensor/lift comparison identify the two composites for a tower of coefficient extensions. Cancel the normalization isomorphisms, using naturality to move them past scalar extension. Transport through the Shrink coefficient square to obtain the tower equation for the actual finite-stage comparisons. This argument applies to every rational object, since its underlying object is an integral object; the normalization is stated on exactly those objects.

For a tower G ≤ H, substitute source transport alpha_A inverse, T(f), alpha_B into the displayed representative at H. Apply the comparison tower equation at A and B. Naturality of the comparison for G ≤ H moves the middle T(f) across it. Cancel the adjacent inverse comparison factors. The canonical target-stage comparison satisfies the tensor-tower associativity equation, so its remaining factors cancel and leave precisely the representative at G. No transition is required to be faithful, and repeated coefficient fields and zero objects obey the same cancellation.
